newsitem.title: FINLAND: WEEK AHEAD - FINLAND TO FOCUS ON EMU PACT, FOMC.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - FINLAND TO FOCUS ON EMU PACT, FOMC.

text.p: Finnish financial markets will focus mainly on the outcome of the Dublin EU summit next week.
The fate of the stability pact and future prospects for convergence on the road towards the third phase of EMU will be carefully studied, analysts said on Friday.
In the U.S., the Federal Reserve's FOMC meeting on Tuesday will be among top issues, as well as U.S. November industrial production and capacity utilisation data, both due on Monday.
At home, November CPI and October industrial production data will be published on Monday, and PPI is due on Wednesday.
DUBLIN EU SUMMIT KEY FOR SENTIMENT
The Dublin EU summit is expected to result in some sort of compromise on the stability pact, analysts said.

"The markets will then have to study what the outcome actually means," said Esko Torsti, chief economist at SE-Banken Helsinki, referring to the level of austerity of the fiscal policies required in EMU.
He added that the market reactions will depend on how market operators actually interpret the nature of the stability pact, which is considered one of the most important issues for EMU.
U.S. KEY INTEREST RATES

The U.S. Federal Reserve is seen holding key interest rates unchanged at its FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) meeting on Tuesday. "Nobody really expects the FED to move the rates," said Jakob Vejloe, head of trading research at Unibank in Copenhagen.
It would be a "super suprise" if the Fed decided to hike rates, Torsti said.

On the stock market, views were mixed about the impact of the FOMC meeting outcome. "If the rates are kept stable, little reaction is expected," said Risto Murto, head of research at brokerage Erik Selin.
Martti Larjo, analyst at Merita Securities, said share prices could turn back into a rise if rates are kept stable.
But if U.S. rates were hiked share prices will get hurt, in Finland, too, analysts said.
U.S. November industrial production and capacity utilisation figures will be published at 1615/1415 GMT on Monday.
FINNISH ECONOMIC INDICATORS
On Monday, the November consumer price index as well as October industrial production will be published by Statistics Finland (SF) at 0700/0500 GMT.
Analysts were mixed on the impact of CPI on the markets.
"If inflation is clearly above one percent, the markets could get nervous," Torsti said, adding interest rates could rise across the yield curve.
But Vejloe at Unibank said that it should take "more than one bad (inflation) figure" in order to move the market as the Bank of Finland had just recently said that the inflation outlook is stable.
In October, headline CPI rose 0.7 percent year-on-year. The mean of five economists' forecasts is 1.0 percent in a 0.9-1.1 percent range.
On the bourse, October industrial production will be an important figure.
"If it turns out to be only four percent it will be bad news," Larjo said.
The mean forecast is for a 7.3 percent year-on-year rise, up from an increase of 6.1 percent in September.
Finnish November producer prices will be released at 0700/0500 GMT on Wednesday.
SCANT DEMAND SEEN FOR BONDS
The State Treasury Office (STO) will auction 9.50-percent 2004 bonds and 8.25-percent 2010 bonds on Thursday.

"The demand (for bonds) is expected to be quite low," said Teijo Rantatupa, market analyst at OKOBANK. STO will auction a maximum amount of 1.50 billion, both maturities considered. The auction outcome will be announced after 1330/1130 GMT.

On Tuesday, STO will issue 85- and 361-day treasury bills in its weekly auction. Torsti at SE-Banken expected solid demand for T-bills. STO's target amount is 1.50 billion markka. The auction result is due after 1330/1130 GMT.
VIKING LINE TO REPORT 12-MTH EARNINGS
Viking Line's full-year results (November-October) are due on December 19 in the morning.
Analysts say the key issue is how Viking Line has managed to boost the profitability of its cruising business.
"The most important issue for the whole sector is how passenger revenue has developed," said Tanja Lounevirta, analyst at Merita Securities.
She referred to both ticket revenue as well as spending onboard.
